lesson.summary: Network cost comes mostly from data transfer and from managed network components that bill per hour and per GB. Keep traffic inside AWS and inside one AZ where you can, use VPC endpoints instead of NAT gateways for AWS services, and cache content at the edge.
keyPoints: Data transfer into AWS is free; data transfer out to the internet and between Regions is charged, and traffic between AZs is charged
NAT gateways bill for each hour they are available and each GB they process; gateway VPC endpoints for S3 and DynamoDB have no hourly or data processing charge
Interface VPC endpoints bill per hour and per GB but can still be cheaper than NAT for heavy AWS service traffic
CloudFront caches content close to users, cutting origin load, and data transfer from AWS origins to CloudFront is free

Direct Connect is billed as port-hour charges plus per-GB data transfer out at a published rate (for example 0.02 USD per GB from a US Region to a US Direct Connect location), with no charge for data transfer in
Transit Gateway and a shared load balancer with path or host rules can replace many peering links and many load balancers

questions.prompt: Instances in private subnets upload several terabytes per month to Amazon S3 in the same Region through a NAT gateway. Which change reduces the data processing cost the most?

options.text: Add a second NAT gateway in another Availability Zone
Replace the NAT gateway with a larger EC2 NAT instance
Move the instances to public subnets with Elastic IP addresses
Create a gateway VPC endpoint for S3 and route S3 traffic through it

questions.explanation: A gateway VPC endpoint for S3 keeps the traffic on the AWS network and has no hourly or per-GB charge, so the NAT data processing fee for S3 traffic disappears. A second NAT gateway adds an hourly charge and does not remove the per-GB processing. A larger NAT instance still moves the traffic over the internet path and adds management work. Public subnets with Elastic IPs expose the instances and still charge for public IPv4 addresses.

questions.prompt: A website serves large static images from an S3 bucket to users worldwide, and data transfer out of S3 is a large part of the bill. Which solution lowers cost and improves latency?

options.text: Put an Amazon CloudFront distribution in front of the bucket
Enable S3 Transfer Acceleration for all downloads
Replicate the bucket to every Region with cross-Region replication
Move the images to S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval

questions.explanation: CloudFront caches objects at edge locations, serves repeat requests from cache, and data transfer from S3 to CloudFront is free, so fewer bytes leave S3 at the higher rate. Transfer Acceleration adds a per-GB fee and targets uploads over long distances. Replicating to every Region multiplies storage and transfer cost. Glacier Instant Retrieval has higher retrieval charges and suits rarely read data, not frequently served images.

questions.prompt: A team wants to reduce data transfer cost for a chatty application where web instances in one AZ call database and cache nodes in other AZs. Which TWO actions reduce cost? (Choose two.)

options.text: Place cache nodes or read replicas in the same AZ as the instances that read from them
Route all internal traffic out through the internet gateway using public IP addresses
Use private IP addresses for communication inside the VPC
Move each tier into a different AWS Region for isolation
Add a NAT gateway so internal calls are translated before leaving the VPC

questions.explanation: Keeping chatty traffic within one AZ avoids cross-AZ data transfer charges, and traffic over private IPs inside the VPC avoids the higher cost of public-address traffic. Sending internal traffic through the internet gateway on public IPs is charged and is less secure. Putting tiers in different Regions adds inter-Region transfer charges. A NAT gateway adds hourly and per-GB charges to traffic that never needed to leave the VPC.

questions.statement: Gateway VPC endpoints are available for Amazon S3 and Amazon DynamoDB and have no additional charge.
questions.explanation: Gateway endpoints are the only endpoint type for S3 and DynamoDB that is free of hourly and data processing charges. Interface endpoints, which use AWS PrivateLink, do incur hourly and per-GB charges.

questions.prompt: Which type of VPC endpoint lets private subnets reach Amazon S3 without a NAT gateway and without hourly or per-GB endpoint charges? Answer with the endpoint type.
questions.explanation: A gateway VPC endpoint is a route table target for S3 and DynamoDB and carries no charge, unlike interface endpoints and NAT gateways.

questions.prompt: A company will move tens of terabytes per month from AWS to its data center, steadily and for years, over a dedicated private connection. Which statement correctly describes how AWS Direct Connect is billed?

options.text: Only per-GB data transfer is charged; the port itself is free
Nothing is charged once the connection has been provisioned
Port-hour charges apply even when idle, plus a per-GB data transfer out charge, while data transfer in is not charged
Data transfer out is billed at the Site-to-Site VPN rate and a flat monthly port fee

questions.explanation: The Direct Connect pricing page describes a bill with two parts: port-hour charges, which apply even when no data is passing through the port, and data transfer out at a per-GB rate (listed as 0.02 USD per GB from a US Region to a US Direct Connect location), with data transfer in at 0.00 USD per GB. Saying only per-GB is charged ignores the port hours, saying nothing is charged after provisioning is wrong, and the pricing page does not tie Direct Connect data transfer to a Site-to-Site VPN rate. For internet comparison, the pricing page points to the EC2 pricing page for internet data transfer out rates.
